title: Call Bayview Community Hospital billing for you?

asks: Apply your insurance: the EOB says you owe $2,600, not $8,700
Show the $500 you already paid, bringing it to $2,100
Ask for the free care under their own policy, bringing the bill to $0 and refunding $500 you overpaid

detail.say: I won't agree to pay anything on the call. Any payment comes back to you first.

speaker: rep
text: Patient Financial Services, this is Diane.

speaker: billback
text: Hello Diane, this is BillBack, an automated assistant calling on behalf of Rosa Martinez, account number BCH-48213977, with her authorization. I'm calling to dispute an incorrect balance on her account from her August 2, 2026 service date.

speaker: rep
text: I show the full balance due on that account.

speaker: billback
text: Diane, the balance shown is $8,700, but the insurer's Explanation of Benefits for claim C-2026-0815-44917 lists the patient responsibility as $2,600. Could you please apply the insurance adjustment so the balance reflects the $2,600 on the EOB?

speaker: rep
text: Hmm, I don't see a payment. What date was it?

speaker: billback
text: A payment of $500 was made on September 14, 2026, with reference number FF2CC2AE. Could you please locate that payment and apply it to the account?

speaker: rep
text: Okay. Can you pay the balance by card today?

speaker: billback
text: I'm not able to make or agree to any payment today. Rosa will review any payment arrangement herself, and I'll follow up. For now, could you please confirm that the insurance adjustment to $2,600 is being applied to the account?

speaker: rep
text: Fine. I'll open a financial assistance review and put a hold on the account. Your case number is FA 20931.

speaker: billback
text: Thank you, Diane. Let me confirm the case number: FA 20931. Before we finish, I'd also like to request that the financial-assistance review apply the hospital's policy, which provides a write-off of the patient responsibility for insured patients at or below 400% of the Federal Poverty Income Guideline with high medical costs. Rosa's income is 149.5% of FPIG and her medical costs exceed 10% of family income, so she appears to qualify, which would bring the balance to $0. Could you confirm that is included in the review?
